# The dependency closure of `mixengine-elevate` built on its own, as `lint` regenerates and diffs it.
# Everything here runs as root. Adding a line is a security decision — see the T40 design, D8, and the
# comment above `[dependencies]` in crates/mixengine-elevate/Cargo.toml.
# Generated on Linux, which is where the `lint` job runs:
#   cargo tree -p mixengine-elevate --no-default-features --edges normal --prefix none --format '{p}' | sed 's/ v[0-9].*//' | sort -u
#
# T49a added two: `pem` and its `base64`. The helper writes MixEngine's authority into an anchors
# directory on Linux and hands it to `security` on macOS, and both of those are PEM text; Windows
# carries DER through its certificate-store API and never sees an envelope, so the dependency is
# declared under `cfg(unix)`. Two crates, measured against the 22 `x509-parser` would have cost and
# the 8 `sha2` would — both of which that task refused, writing its own DER reader instead. What
# these buy is base64 padding rules nobody should hand-write, at the version `rcgen` pins so the
# workspace holds one copy. See the T49a design, D11.
#
# T88a added one: `minisign-verify`, and it brings nothing with it — the crate has no dependencies of
# its own and vendors the Ed25519 and Blake2b it needs. It is what checks a replacement helper inside
# the elevated process, against a key compiled into the copy already installed, which is the single
# rule `.claude/features/updates.md` calls the most important on its page. Weighed against the eight
# crates `sha2` would have cost, which is the trade T49a refused two paragraphs up.
base64
itoa
libc
memchr
minisign-verify
mixengine-elevate
mixengine-platform
mixengine-proto
pem
proc-macro2
quote
serde
serde_core
serde_derive
serde_json
syn
thiserror

zmij
